question.title: Food Delivery Read Write Database Architecture
question.description: Separate write traffic onto a replicated primary and read traffic onto lag-aware replicas while maintaining a bounded strong single-key consistency proxy.
question.author: Hritvik Mohan

prompt.text: Extend the event-driven platform with a read-heavy relational workload. Send writes to a primary database and distribute reads to replicas. Configure replication and handle replica lag without returning stale values in the hidden single-key workload. This simulator verifies a bounded single-key register history; it does not prove multi-key transactional consistency.
prompt.additionalContext: The hidden run is a deterministic, scaled discrete proxy for the stated production workload. It grades supported simulator behavior, not cloud-provider guarantees.

functionalRequirements.text: Send writes to a primary database.
Send reads to at least two read replicas.
Never return stale data from a replica, even while replication lags.
Keep the API Gateway, event stream, load-balanced order path, and queue from the previous designs.

dryRunCase.description: A low-rate public run for checking connectivity and request flow.

scenarios.description: Run an 80/20 read/write mix through two lagged strong-read replicas and a primary-acknowledged write leader.

structuralRules.description: Keep every component connected to the architecture.
Keep the API Gateway from the previous design.
Keep the event stream from the previous design.

semanticRules.description: Place the load balancer between incoming traffic and the application servers.
Place the queue between the order service and a background worker that consumes it.
Place the event stream between the producing services and the consumers that read it.
Configure a database as the replication primary for writes.
Include at least two read replicas.
Configure at least two databases as read replicas.

rubricChecks.description: Reads must be served by replicas that catch up on replication lag.
No read may return stale data.
